observed_from: an -Apply of asset-server/Deploy-GeneratedAssets.ps1, which uploads through a staging directory, re-hashes every file remotely, probes the rebuilt image on a throwaway root, and only then recreates the services
hash_convention: repo_sha256 is the repository blob (git cat-file blob HEAD:<repo_source>), i.e. the bytes a clean checkout deploys; deployed_sha256 is the file on the NAS.

generated-assets.role: one release, verified per request; official original for anything it does not translate

generated-assets-sync.role: keeps that one release in step with the repository, holding a single-writer lock

note: The distributor now holds exactly one release: assets_route.py and sync_loop.py were replaced by serve_release.py and sync_release.py, both shipped from this repository and removed from the NAS project directory by the same -Apply that recorded this. scripts/assets_mirror.py is no longer part of this deployment; the archive deployment (asset-server/docker-compose.yml) still builds it, because mirroring many official versions is that deployment's job.
verification: asset-server/generated-assets/test_closure.py reads this file: the recorded repository blobs must exist at HEAD, the hashes must match the deployed bytes where repo_matches_deployed is true, and the image and compose contracts must describe the programs actually started. The live route was also compared byte for byte against its predecessor before the switch.
